title: Universal derivation of the principal quotient Roos functor on K-flat complexes
statement: On a site essentially small in the coefficient universe, let R be a sheaf of commutative rings and t a global section. If countable products of R-module sheaves are exact, the ordinary quotient Roos functor [def-pur-principal-quotient-completion-model] admits a universal left derived functor whose counit is invertible on every K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. No augmentation or completion unit is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 0941; the indicated explicit steps of lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange.

proof.text: Tensor homotopies with the fixed quotient complexes and assemble using their transition maps. Taking products and the signed cone preserves those homotopies, so quotientRoos followed by localization factors through the homotopy category. Use the existing strict Roos compatible-homotopy theorem for the final products and cone.

For a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes, compare each fixed quotient with a K-flat resolution. Tensor cancellation and two-out-of-three show that each level is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact countable products and the cone triangle imply the same for its Roos map.

K-flat resolutions give a resolving class on the homotopy category. Apply resolving-class essential constancy and the pointwise Kan bridge to obtain a total left derived functor. The identity resolution proves counit invertibility on each K-flat object. Transport the universal pair through the full essentially surjective homotopy quotient and quotientCompQhIso. Only the general essential-constancy and Kan-extension assertions are used; the quotient Roos functor does not need to be equipped with a triangulated-functor instance for this universal-pair construction.

proof_origin.place: Explicit refinement of the balanced quotient and resolving-class arguments in lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange.

theorem exists_derivedQuotientRoos
    (t : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)).sections)
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ)
      (ringedSiteModules.{r} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))] :
    ∃ (L : DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
        (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
          (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)))
      (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L ⟶ quotientRoos R t ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)) ∧
        ∀ P, CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := R) P →
          IsIso (ε.app P)
